status.summary: UFC women's bantamweight champion. She won the title with a kimura from side control at 4:55 of round 2 against Julianna Pena at UFC 316 in Newark (Jun 7, 2025), her last fight. Her first defence, against the returning Amanda Nunes at UFC 324 (Jan 24, 2026), was postponed nine days out when she had neck surgery for herniated discs in New York (a two-level cervical fusion). She returned to full training in late August and now defends against Nunes in the co-main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden on Nov 14, 2026, with Joselyne Edwards as the backup fighter. She has said she feels 'awesome' and has talked about possibly retiring after the Nunes fight, without deciding. Two-time Olympic judo champion (2012, 2016) and two-time PFL lightweight tournament winner. Pro record 19-1; UFC 3-0.

style.summary: A control grappler from a judo background (two Olympic judo golds, 2012 and 2016, per Sherdog and Wikipedia's UFC 334 page). She closes to the clinch, takes opponents down, holds them there (533 s of control per 15 min, decayed) and strikes or hunts submissions from top. Opponents have not taken her down (0 of 2 attempts) and land only 1.1 significant strikes per minute on her.

moves.notes: Weights are relative within each target group, as src/director.js uses them: head moves sum to 1, body to 1, legs to 1. spinning, knee and elbow are separate rates for occasional specials. In fighters.json her decayed significant attempts go 78.3% head, 14.4% body and 7.3% legs (landed 69.4/21.1/9.5). That is close to the women's bantamweight average of 75.9/14.8/9.3, with slightly fewer leg kicks. By position, 39% of her attempts come on the ground and 13% in the clinch (division 8% and 9%). The director draws those from its own clinch and ground tables. No web scouting source could be read in this pass, and ufcstats does not log strike types, so the within-group splits are judgement. The head group is a punch-led split with few head kicks, to fit a grappler striking to close distance. Punches lead the body group because her body strikes land at 90%, which suggests close range. Legs are split evenly because the data cannot tell calf kicks from inside kicks. knee 0.25 and elbow 0.20 are judgement for her clinch and top work. Three fights is a tiny sample. Low confidence.

Opponents land 1.1 significant strikes per minute on her at 34% accuracy (decayed). She lands 4.1 per minute at 61%, but half of those land on the ground.

Sample warning: 3 UFC fights (31.7 min), and only one went past round 2. Her round 2 rate (2.8 times round 1) comes from a single fight. The engine should shrink her rates firmly toward the division prior. Her decayed Elo of 1619 is held down by the short record.
She has no knockdowns scored or absorbed in the UFC. Both finishes are submissions from dominant top positions: a rear-naked choke on Holm and a kimura from side control on Pena.
